$$y=e^{2x}\tan x$$
Using the product rule, $y'=u'v+v'u$, with
$$\begin{aligned}u&=e^{2x} & v&=\tan x\\u'&=2e^{2x} & v'&=\sec^2 x\end{aligned}$$
$$y'=2e^{2x}\tan x+e^{2x}\sec^2 x$$

solutions.latex:
$$y=\dfrac{4x}{\cos 3x}$$
Using the quotient rule, $y'=\dfrac{u'v-v'u}{v^2}$, with
$$\begin{aligned}u&=4x & v&=\cos 3x\\u'&=4 & v'&=-3\sin 3x\end{aligned}$$
$$y'=\dfrac{4\cos 3x+12x\sin 3x}{(\cos 3x)^2}$$
solutions.marks_breakdown: 2: correct solution; 1: correctly attempts to use the quotient rule, or equivalent merit

solutions.latex:
$$\begin{aligned}f(x)&=e^{2x+1}x^4\\f'(x)&=2e^{2x+1}x^4+4x^3e^{2x+1}\\f''(x)&=4e^{2x+1}x^4+8x^3e^{2x+1}+12x^2e^{2x+1}+8x^3e^{2x+1}\\f''(x)&=4e^{2x+1}x^4+16x^3e^{2x+1}+12x^2e^{2x+1}\end{aligned}$$
Let $f'(x)=0$:
$$\begin{aligned}0&=2x^3e^{2x+1}(x+2)\\x&=0,\ -2\end{aligned}$$
$f''(0)=0$, so $x=0$ is a potential point of inflection.

$f''(-2)=-0.79\ldots<0$, so maximum point.

$\therefore$ maximum point at $(-2,\ 0.79\ldots)$

Test $(0,0)$:

\extable{317_q28_t1}

$\therefore$ $(0,0)$ is a minimum stationary point.

Since $y=(x-4)^2$, when $x=0$, $y=16$, so $C(0,16)$.

\exfigure{317_q29_s1}

Find the area of the whole trapezium, subtract the area of the rectangle and subtract the area under the curve from $x=0$ to $x=2$.
$$\text{Trapezium}=\dfrac{16+4}{2}\times 6=60$$
$$\text{Rectangle}=4\times 4=16$$
$$\begin{aligned}\text{Area under the curve}&=\int_0^2(x-4)^2\,dx\\&=\int_0^2 x^2-8x+16\,dx\\&=\left[\dfrac{1}{3}x^3-4x^2+16x\right]_0^2\\&=\dfrac{8}{3}-16+32\\&=\dfrac{56}{3}\end{aligned}$$
$$\begin{aligned}\therefore\ \text{shaded area}&=60-16-\dfrac{56}{3}\\&=\dfrac{76}{3}\end{aligned}$$
